doc.title: Ben Sidran interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 15, 2023

title: The Wurlitzer electric piano
summary: The Wurlitzer predates the Rhodes, used by Ray Charles and Zawinul, giving keyboardists a volume control.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: There’s the Wurlitzer piano shows up in a number of your videos. Did they have Wurlitzer piano over there?

Yeah. Yeah. They had everything. And the Wurlitzer was before the Fender Rhodes. It was the first electric keyboard. You know that’s the one Ray Charles played on “What’d I Say” that just blew everybody’s mind.

Yes. Yes. And it was the first opportunity for a keyboard player to have a volume control. You know the guitar players had volume, but keyboard players had a microphone stuck in an upright piano. You know it wasn’t fair competition. The Wurlitzer was great.
